Autumn's Surrender

Once-defiant apples
    now surrender to the pot,
their tart rebellion melting
into sweet submission

Yesterday's firm soldiers
    tumble and spin
in cinnamon storms, drowning
in their own essence
        while sugar crystals
        plot their sticky coup

Who knew revolution
could taste this good?
    flesh yielding
    to heat's persistent sermon

Until what was crisp
becomes memory —
    a soft, warm whisper
    of what autumn meant to be
